description:
Confirms 05-11's OWN LITERAL demonstration steps exactly as a real learner would run them (advisor-review, 2026-09-27) - NOT the isolated/ticket-1-fixed variant part05-mch1202-corrupt uses. Compiles the AS-SHIPPED src/legacy/qclsrc/ju0900c.clp and AS-SHIPPED src/legacy/qrpgsrc/za0500.rpg. Runs C0511S (05-11's own technique) to plant JUNO=C05119 into JUCHUD/JUCHUM, then CALLs JU0900C.

REVISION 2 (2026-09-27, after this manifest's own first connection contaminated its result and got fixed at the source): the first connection unexpectedly raised a real decimal-data error (`ZA0500 6400 decimal-data error`, RPG0907) even though C0511S at the time planted 'ABCDE' (already confirmed, in isolation, to read silently as 12345 with no error). Root cause: C0511S's own DELETE only removed WHERE JUNO='C05119' from JUBADD, but its CPYF copies the WHOLE file - a prior investigative manifest (part05-decimal-screen) had left 4 leftover rows in JUBADD (JUNO='C0513x', digit-nibble-invalid values), which got silently re-planted into JUCHUD alongside C05119. The FIRST row OPNQRYF's ascending order actually delivered was still C05119 ('ABCDE', digit nibbles 1-5, valid) - so the statement-6400 error was almost certainly raised by one of the C0513x rows read immediately after it, not by this manifest's own intended C05119 row. FIXED: C0511S's DELETE is now a blanket DELETE FROM JUBADD (a real latent bug, not just a test-contamination fluke - see that file's own header), and it now plants JUSU='.....' (5 periods, EBCDIC X'4B', digit nibble B - genuinely invalid, unlike 'ABCDE'/blanks which both have valid digit nibbles) instead of 'ABCDE'. This manifest now re-confirms the CORRECTED, uncontaminated scenario: with JUBADD holding ONLY the intended C05119 row, does '.....' alone raise the same statement-6400 RPG0907 that the contaminated run showed? Two new collect steps (JUBADD row count, JUCHUD C0513x row count) directly verify no contamination this time.

Self-containment: same CHKOBJ+conditional/DLTPGM-first idioms as sibling part05-* manifests. RUNTXRESET first (shared &LIB defensive reasoning) - TXRESET itself worked correctly in the contaminated first run (it resets JUCHUD/JUCHUM/ZAIKOM to their standard 12/8/6-row dataset); the contamination was introduced AFTER TXRESET, by C0511S's own CPYF step copying stale leftover rows out of JUBADD (a file TXRESET does not touch, and is not supposed to - it is C0511S's own transient staging file). Prerequisite: TXSETUP has already built the sample DB in this library; run from a branch where src/qclsrc/c0511s.clp, src/legacy/qddssrc/jubadd.pf, src/legacy/qclsrc/ju0900c.clp, src/legacy/qrpgsrc/za0500.rpg all exist.

steps.label: CPC0511RUN
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511RUN)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511RUN) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(C0511RUN) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPC0511S
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511S)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511S) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(C0511S) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPJU0900C
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/JU0900C)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/JU0900C) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(JU0900C) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPZA0500
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/ZA0500)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTRPGPGM PGM(&LIB/ZA0500) SRCFILE(&LIB/QRPGSRC) SRCMBR(ZA0500) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS STRAY_ROWS FROM &LIB/JUCHUD WHERE JUNO LIKE 'C0513%'
SELECT JUNO, JULINE, JUSHO, JUSU, HEX(JUSU) AS JUSU_HEX, JUTNK FROM &LIB/JUCHUD WHERE JUNO = 'C05119'
SELECT JUNO, JULINE, JUSHO, JUSU FROM &LIB/JUCHUD ORDER BY JUNO, JULINE
SELECT JUNO FROM &LIB/JUCHUM ORDER BY JUNO
SELECT ZASHO, ZASU, ZAUPD FROM &LIB/ZAIKOM WHERE ZASHO = 'P00001'
